label: HOPX/OLFM1 excitatory neuronal niche
function: Likely a mature cortical neuronal region with an HOPX/OLFM1-associated transcriptional state, potentially corresponding to a corticocortical or intratelencephalic neuron population. CAMK2N1 and HPCAL1 support differentiated neuronal signaling and calcium-dependent activity.

label: Myelinated excitatory neuron niche
function: This appears to be a mixed neuronal–oligodendrocyte niche, with strong myelin-associated expression alongside SLC17A7-positive excitatory neurons. It likely represents cortical axons/excitatory neuronal processes embedded in a myelinated white-matter-like environment rather than a pure cell population.

label: Large axon-rich neuronal niche
function: A strongly neuronal, axon-rich region characterized by abundant neurofilament proteins, consistent with large-caliber neuronal processes and mature neuronal architecture. The mitochondrial genes suggest high energetic demand from these processes, although their prominence also lowers confidence somewhat.

label: Synaptic cortical neuron niche
function: A neuronal and synapse-rich cortical niche with strong expression of presynaptic machinery and neuronal cytoskeletal genes. The presence of STMN1 may indicate a particular neuronal state or immature/repair-associated cytoskeletal program, but the overall profile is clearly dominated by neuronal signaling.

label: Myelinated glial niche
function: A strongly oligodendrocyte/myelin-associated niche, consistent with white-matter-like tissue or heavily myelinated cortical processes. GFAP, S100B and PTGDS indicate an astroglial component, suggesting close spatial association between oligodendrocytes and astrocytes.

label: Astrocyte-rich metabolic niche
function: A predominantly astrocytic niche associated with extracellular glutamate handling and metabolic support of nearby neurons. SLC1A2 and GFAP strongly support astrocyte identity, while the abundance of mitochondrial transcripts may reflect metabolically active astrocytes but also introduces some technical/quality uncertainty.

label: HOPX/OLFM1 cortical neuronal niche
function: Likely a superficial cortical neuronal region, consistent with dendritic and synaptic processing in the upper layers of DLPFC. HOPX and OLFM1 support a superficial/early-layer neuronal identity, while CAMK2N1 and HPCAL1 indicate mature excitatory neuronal signaling.

label: Oligodendrocyte-associated excitatory neuronal niche
function: This appears to be an oligodendrocyte-rich niche with an admixture of excitatory neuronal signal, potentially near a gray-matter/white-matter interface or along myelinated cortical processes. MBP and PLP1 strongly support myelinating glia, whereas SLC17A7 indicates excitatory neurons; KRT17 and SCGB2A2 are unusual for adult DLPFC and lower confidence in a clean biological interpretation.

label: Myelinated neuronal/axonal niche
function: Likely represents a region enriched for neuronal somata and especially large-caliber axons or neuronal processes, potentially deeper cortical layers or tissue near white matter. The strong NEFL/NEFM/NEFH program indicates structural neuronal processes rather than a specific cortical-layer identity.

label: Active cortical neuronal niche
function: A neuronal-rich cortical region engaged in synaptic transmission and neuronal structural remodeling. PCP4 is compatible with mature cortical neurons, while SNAP25, SYT1, SYN2 and SNCB indicate abundant synaptic machinery; STMN1/STMN2 suggest cytoskeletal remodeling or a subset of less mature/stressed neurons.

label: Myelinated white-matter glial niche
function: This is most consistent with a white-matter or strongly myelinated region, dominated by mature oligodendrocytes with an astrocytic component. MBP, PLP1, CNP and MOBP form a strong myelin program, while GFAP, S100B and PTGDS indicate associated astrocytes and glial support of axonal tissue.

label: Astrocyte-rich cortical niche
function: This is a clear astrocyte-rich niche, likely representing cortical parenchyma with strong metabolic and extracellular-homeostasis support. SLC1A2 indicates glutamate uptake, while GFAP, CST3 and CLU support an astrocytic/reactive-support program; the many mitochondrial genes may partly reflect technical or energetic-state variation rather than a distinct anatomical region.

label: HOPX/OLFM1 excitatory neuronal niche
function: Likely a differentiated cortical neuronal region enriched for HOPX and OLFM1, consistent with a specialized excitatory-neuron population involved in cortical circuit signaling. The strong mitochondrial representation reduces confidence somewhat.

label: Mixed myelinated-neuron niche
function: This appears to be a mixed niche containing myelinating oligodendrocytes together with excitatory neurons rather than a clean anatomical region. MBP/PLP1 suggest local myelin support, while SLC17A7 and SYT1 indicate glutamatergic neuronal signaling.

label: Axon-rich neuronal niche
function: An axon- and cytoskeleton-rich neuronal niche, consistent with dense neuronal processes and projection fibers. The abundance of neurofilament genes suggests prominent axonal structure and maintenance rather than a specific cortical laminar identity.

label: Active synaptic neuronal niche
function: A neuronal signaling niche characterized by synaptic machinery and neuronal cytoskeletal genes, consistent with active local synaptic communication and remodeling of neuronal processes. STMN1/STMN2 additionally suggest cytoskeletal dynamics and neuronal process maintenance.

label: Mature oligodendrocyte/myelin niche
function: A strongly myelinated glial niche dominated by mature oligodendrocytes, with accompanying astrocytic signatures. It likely supports axonal insulation, myelin maintenance, and metabolic/homeostatic support of nearby neurons.

label: Astrocytic homeostatic niche
function: A predominantly astrocytic niche involved in extracellular homeostasis, neurotransmitter clearance, and metabolic support of neurons. The high mitochondrial content may indicate elevated metabolic activity or stressed/damaged cells, but the SLC1A2/GFAP/CST3/CLU combination provides strong biological support for astrocytes.

label: Excitatory neuron / oligodendrocyte-interface niche
function: This appears to be a neuronal niche with strong excitatory glutamatergic identity, likely adjacent to or intermingled with myelinated axons. The combination suggests active synaptic signaling in a cortical gray-matter region with substantial oligodendrocyte influence.

label: Mature oligodendrocyte / white-matter niche
function: This is a clear myelinating glial niche, consistent with white matter or a gray-white matter interface. Its main activity is axonal myelination and maintenance, with some astrocytic contribution.

label: Neuronal axon-rich niche
function: This is a neuron-dense region dominated by neuronal structural and axonal machinery. It likely represents neuropil-rich cortical tissue supporting axonal transport, neuronal signaling, and synaptic connectivity rather than a specific glial compartment.

label: Astrocyte-rich glial niche
function: This is most consistent with an astrocyte-rich cortical glial region, with signatures of extracellular/lipid homeostasis and potentially local glial activation. The abundance of mitochondrial transcripts lowers confidence somewhat because it may partly reflect tissue quality or cellular stress rather than a distinct biological niche.

label: HOPX+ CCK cortical interneuron niche
function: This is a neuronal niche with a strong HOPX/CCK/OLFM1 signature, consistent with a specialized cortical neuronal population and likely GABAergic interneuron-associated circuitry. It appears metabolically active and involved in local circuit modulation rather than myelination or generalized glial support.

label: HOPX+/OLFM1 neuronal niche with mitochondrial signal
function: The non-mitochondrial markers suggest a neuronal population related to niche_4, potentially another HOPX+/OLFM1 cortical neuronal state or layer-associated compartment. However, the marker list is overwhelmingly mitochondrial, so it is difficult to distinguish a genuine biological niche from a metabolically stressed or technically biased region.

label: Excitatory cortical–myelinated interface
function: This looks like a cortical gray-matter niche enriched for excitatory neuronal signaling, with substantial nearby or overlapping myelinated processes. SLC17A7, SNAP25 and SYT1 support active glutamatergic neurons, while MBP may reflect oligodendrocyte/process contribution at a gray–white matter interface.

label: Oligodendrocyte-rich white matter
function: This is a strongly myelinating glial niche, most consistent with white matter or a heavily myelinated cortical region. Oligodendrocytes are producing and maintaining myelin around axons, with GFAP/S100B indicating some astrocytic contribution.

label: Neuronal axon-rich cortex
function: This is a neuron-dense niche dominated by neuronal cytoskeletal and synaptic machinery, consistent with cortical gray matter containing abundant neuronal processes and axons. The markers indicate active neuronal maintenance and signaling rather than a specialized glial compartment.

label: Astrocyte-rich cortical glia
function: This represents an astrocyte-rich glial niche involved in extracellular homeostasis, neurotransmitter clearance and metabolic support of nearby neurons. The strong SLC1A2, CST3 and CLU signal is much more biologically informative than the mitochondrial enrichment.

label: HOPX/CCK superficial cortical neurons
function: This appears to be a superficial cortical neuronal niche, likely involving HOPX/OLFM1-positive layer 2/3 populations with a CCK-positive interneuron component. It is therefore likely associated with local cortical processing and intracortical synaptic integration rather than white-matter functions.

label: Mitochondria-rich HOPX/OLFM1 neurons
function: The HOPX/OLFM1/ENC1 signature suggests a neuronal niche related to the superficial cortical populations seen in niche 4, but the marker list is overwhelmingly mitochondrial. It may represent metabolically active neurons, but the unusually strong mitochondrial signal makes technical/quality effects a substantial alternative explanation.

label: Excitatory neuron–myelin interface
function: This looks like a neuronal region adjacent to or intermingled with myelinated processes, with active excitatory neurotransmission and substantial axonal/myelin support. The mixed neuronal and oligodendrocyte signature suggests a gray–white matter interface or neuropil-rich niche rather than a pure cell layer.

label: Oligodendrocyte-rich white matter
function: This is a strongly myelinating glial niche, consistent with white matter or a myelin-rich tract. Oligodendrocytes are supporting and maintaining myelinated axons, while the accompanying astrocytic markers suggest metabolic and homeostatic support.

label: Neuronal axon/synapse-rich cortex
function: This is a neuron-dense, neuropil-rich region characterized by neuronal cytoskeleton, axonal machinery, and synaptic signaling. It likely represents cortical gray matter with substantial neuronal processes rather than a specific glial compartment.

label: Astrocytic homeostatic niche
function: This is most consistent with an astrocyte-rich region involved in extracellular homeostasis, neurotransmitter clearance, and metabolic support of nearby neurons. The strong SLC1A2 and CST3/CLU signature supports a homeostatic/reactive-leaning astroglial compartment.

label: HOPX/OLFM1 cortical neuronal layer
function: This appears to be a neuronal cortical gray-matter niche with a HOPX/OLFM1-associated identity, consistent with superficial cortical neuronal populations. CCK and CYP46A1 suggest specialized neuronal signaling and cholesterol metabolism, respectively.

label: Mitochondrial-rich HOPX/OLFM1 neurons
function: The non-mitochondrial markers point toward the same HOPX/OLFM1 neuronal cortical compartment as niche_4, but the marker list is dominated by mitochondrial transcripts. This could reflect metabolically active neurons, but the heavy mitochondrial signal also raises concern for low-quality/stressed tissue or technical variation, so the regional assignment is less secure.

function: Likely a gray matter region of mixed neuronal and glial composition (possibly superficial layers), with synaptic/neuronal activity signals. The prominent mitochondrial genes suggest a partly technical or metabolic-density driven cluster, so the biological assignment is tentative.

label: Gray-white matter boundary / deep layer 6 with myelinated fibers
function: A transitional zone where myelinated axon bundles intermix with glutamatergic projection neurons, supporting long-range signal conduction and axonal insulation. Some markers (SCGB2A2, KRT17) are unusual for cortex and may reflect ambient/spurious signal.

label: Layer 5 large projection neuron zone
function: Deep cortical layer rich in large long-projecting pyramidal neurons with heavy neurofilament cytoskeletons and high energy demand for axonal conduction. Mitochondrial genes are consistent with metabolically demanding neurons but also temper confidence.

label: Upper cortical layers (L2/3) synapse-rich neuropil
function: Dense neuronal and synaptic region in superficial/mid cortex involved in intracortical processing, synaptic transmission and plasticity, with active cytoskeletal remodeling.

label: Subcortical white matter
function: Myelinated axon tract region where oligodendrocytes maintain myelin sheaths for fast conduction, with fibrous astrocytes providing structural and metabolic support.

label: Cortical layer 1 / pial-adjacent astrocyte-rich zone
function: Astrocyte-dominated region (likely layer 1 / glia limitans or astrocyte-rich cortex) handling glutamate clearance and metabolic support. Strong mitochondrial and MALAT1 signals suggest partial technical contribution, lowering confidence.

label: Mixed cortical grey matter / low-specificity niche (likely deep-layer or pia-adjacent)
function: Likely a heterogeneous grey matter zone combining neuronal signalling and astrocytic support. The marker list is dominated by mitochondrial transcripts, so the signal reflects metabolic or technical variation (RNA quality, capture depth) as much as true region identity.

label: Deep cortical layers / grey-white matter boundary (layer 6 plus myelinated fibres)
function: A transition zone where deep-layer glutamatergic neurons sit among myelinated axon bundles, supporting excitatory output and myelination. Contains some likely contamination or ambient signal.

label: Layer 5 (large pyramidal neuron) cortex
function: Energetically demanding output layer with large long-range projection neurons rich in neurofilaments and oxidative phosphorylation machinery, sending signals to subcortical targets.

label: Upper cortical layers (layers 2/3 to 4) neuropil
function: Dense synaptic and cytoskeletal-remodelling zone supporting intracortical processing and plasticity among superficial pyramidal neurons.

label: Cortical white matter
function: Myelinated axon tract carrying cortico-cortical and subcortical connections, maintained by oligodendrocytes with supporting fibrous astrocytes and iron handling.

label: Astrocyte-rich layer 1 / glia limitans or perivascular grey matter
function: Astrocyte-dominated zone handling glutamate clearance, metabolic support and glial scaffolding, consistent with superficial layer 1 or vessel-adjacent cortex. Mitochondrial and MALAT1 signals lower confidence.

label: Mixed cortical neuropil / likely layer-boundary or technical-signal-dominated niche
function: Likely a cortical grey-matter zone combining neuronal and astrocytic signal, with a strong mitochondrial component suggesting high-metabolic-density neuropil or capture/RNA-quality effects. The biology is weakly resolved and should be treated cautiously.

label: Deep cortical layers / grey-white matter transition (layer 6 with myelinated fibers)
function: A transition zone where deep-layer glutamatergic neurons sit alongside myelinated axon tracts, supporting synaptic transmission and axonal myelination. Oligodendrocyte signal reflects myelinated projections entering the white matter.

label: Layer 5 large pyramidal neuron band (long-projection neurons)
function: A zone rich in large projection neurons with heavily neurofilament-laden axons and high energetic demand, supporting long-range cortical output and rapid action potential conduction.

label: Upper cortical layers (layers 2/3) synapse-dense neuropil
function: Synapse-rich superficial cortex involved in cortico-cortical integration, with active synaptic vesicle cycling, calcium signaling, and neurite/cytoskeletal remodeling.

label: Subcortical white matter
function: Myelinated axon tract region where oligodendrocytes maintain and insulate long-range fibers, with fibrous astrocytes providing metabolic and structural support.

label: Layer 1 / pial-adjacent astrocyte-rich zone (possible mixed with technical signal)
function: Astrocyte-dominated superficial region involved in glutamate clearance and neuropil support, likely layer 1 or glia limitans. Mitochondrial and MALAT1 signals add ambiguity and may reflect technical or abundance effects.

label: Astrocyte-rich glial region (cortical layer 1 / pial surface)
Upper-layer cortex (layers 1-3) with superficial excitatory neurons and pia/meningeal edge
function: Glutamatergic neuron-rich superficial cortex that supports cortico-cortical synaptic transmission and local integration. The KRT17/DKK3 signal together with MBP suggests the niche touches the pial surface or subpial layer 1.

label: White matter (myelinated fiber tracts) with fibrous astrocytes
function: Axon-bundle region where oligodendrocytes maintain myelin sheaths for fast signal conduction between cortical areas and subcortical targets. Astrocytes provide metabolic and structural support and respond to iron and stress.

label: Deep-layer cortex (layers 5-6) with large projection neurons
function: Neuron-dense layer enriched in large pyramidal neurons that send long-range axons to subcortical and distal targets. The high cytoskeletal and neurofilament content reflects heavy axonal investment and high metabolic demand.

label: Astrocyte-rich glial/neuropil niche (likely pial-adjacent layer 1 or perivascular region)
function: Astrocyte-dominated territory handling glutamate clearance, extracellular homeostasis and metabolic support of synapses. The heavy mitochondrial signal suggests a partly low-complexity, technical or metabolic-state contribution, so the exact anatomical position is uncertain.

label: Mid-layer cortex (layers 3-5) with excitatory neurons, CCK+ pyramidal neurons
function: Intermediate cortical layers where excitatory neurons integrate inputs and modulate activity via CaMKII regulation and neuropeptide signaling. Plasticity and calcium-handling genes point to synaptically active neuropil.

label: Mitochondria-dominated neuronal grey matter (likely cortical layer neuropil; low confidence)
function: Energetically active grey matter neuropil, but the top markers are mostly mitochondrial-encoded genes, so the signal may reflect transcript abundance, capture depth or tissue quality rather than a distinct biological domain. It likely overlaps with niche_4 and represents a metabolically high or technically biased sub-population of the same layers.

label: Upper cortical layers (L2/3 and layer 1 boundary) with excitatory neurons
function: Glutamatergic projection neurons in superficial cortex carrying out synaptic transmission and corticocortical signaling. The DIRAS2/KRT17/DKK3 signal suggests proximity to the upper layers and possibly the layer 1/pial boundary, with MBP reflecting some intracortical myelin or contamination from adjacent white matter.

label: Subcortical white matter (with reactive/fibrous astrocytes)
function: Myelinated axon tracts carrying signals between cortex and other brain regions, maintained by oligodendrocytes that produce and sustain myelin. Astrocyte markers indicate fibrous astrocytes supporting the tracts, plus iron handling and metabolic support.

label: Deep cortical layers (L5/6) with large projection neurons
function: Deep-layer projection neurons with large, neurofilament-rich axons that send output to subcortical and distant targets. High cytoskeletal and synaptic gene expression reflects energetically demanding axon maintenance and active neurotransmission.

label: Astrocyte-rich glial niche (likely layer 1 / pial-adjacent or glia-dominated cortex)
function: Astrocyte-dominated tissue handling glutamate clearance and metabolic support of synapses. The strong mitochondrial component suggests high metabolic activity but also may partly reflect technical/capture bias, so region assignment is tentative.

label: Mid-cortical layers (L4/L5-like) excitatory neuron niche
function: Excitatory neurons in intermediate cortical layers involved in receiving and relaying cortical signals. Expression of activity- and layer-associated genes suggests active synaptic and calcium signaling, with a mitochondrial component that is partly technical.

label: Neuron-rich cortical niche dominated by mitochondrial signal (likely technical/metabolic artifact)
function: Likely gray-matter neuronal tissue with high oxidative metabolism, but most top markers are mitochondrial-encoded genes, which commonly reflect capture bias, cell quality, or sequencing depth rather than a distinct region. The niche shares ENC1/HOPX/OLFM1 with niche_4, suggesting a related neuronal layer with a technical overlay.

label: Layer 1 / pial-adjacent superficial cortex (meninges-glia limitans with upper-layer neurons)
function: Superficial cortex at the pial boundary, mixing glutamatergic upper-layer neuron signal (synaptic transmission, axon growth) with pial/meningeal and myelin-associated signal. The region integrates long-range inputs and supports cortical surface barrier functions.

label: Subcortical white matter
function: Myelinated axon tracts carrying signals between cortical areas and to subcortical targets, maintained by oligodendrocytes (myelin production) and fibrous astrocytes (metabolic and structural support, iron handling).

label: Deep cortical layers (L5/L6 projection neuron zone)
function: Deep cortical layers with large neurofilament-rich projection neurons that send long-range axons to subcortical and other cortical targets. Reflects high cytoskeletal and axonal maintenance demands and excitatory output.

label: Glia-rich / vascular-associated zone (astrocyte-dominated, likely layer 1 or perivascular)
function: Astrocyte-dominated tissue handling glutamate clearance and metabolic support of neurons. Mitochondrial gene enrichment suggests high energy metabolism and some technical/quality contribution, so interpretation is less certain.

label: Mid-cortical layers (L3-L5 excitatory neuron zone)
function: Intermediate cortical layers rich in excitatory pyramidal neurons carrying out local and cortico-cortical processing, with calcium signaling and plasticity-related activity. Mitochondrial genes add some metabolic or technical signal.

label: Metabolically active neuron-rich cortex (likely upper/mid layers; mitochondria-dominated signal)
function: Neuron-dense gray matter with high oxidative phosphorylation demand, closely resembling niche_4. The strong mitochondrial-gene dominance means the cluster may partly reflect a technical or capture-depth axis rather than a distinct biological region.
